title: Arrest and detention — general guidance
citation: Constitution of Kenya, 2010, Art. 49; Criminal Procedure Code
content: Arrested persons have rights: to be informed of reasons, to remain silent, to legal representation, to be brought before court within 24 hours, and to bail or bond where applicable. Police must not use excessive force. Note the station, OB number, officers involved, and time of arrest.

title: Assault and theft — general guidance
content: Assault and theft are criminal offences. Victims should report to police, obtain medical attention and a P3 form where injured, and keep records such as photos, receipts, and witness contacts. The Director of Public Prosecutions handles prosecution.

title: Bail and bond — general guidance
citation: Constitution of Kenya, 2010, Art. 49; Criminal Procedure Code
content: An arrested or accused person has the right to bail or bond on reasonable conditions unless there are compelling reasons to deny it. Conditions and amounts vary by offence and court. Keep bail receipts, surety documents, and hearing dates, and confirm conditions with the court or lawyer.

title: Appealing a criminal conviction or sentence
content: Convictions and sentences can be appealed within short statutory timelines. Get the judgment, proceedings, and charge sheet immediately and brief counsel. Keep filing receipts and bail-pending-appeal papers where applicable.

title: Arson and property destruction
content: Deliberately setting fire to buildings, crops, or vehicles is arson with severe penalties. Report immediately, preserve the scene for investigators, and list destroyed property with values. Keep photos and ownership documents.

title: Assault occasioning actual bodily harm
content: Fights causing injury should be reported with a P3 form for medical documentation. Get treatment first, then the police issue the P3 for the doctor to complete. Keep treatment notes, photos, and witness contacts.

title: Reviewing harsh bail or bond terms
content: Accused persons unable to meet bail can apply for review with reasons and surety details. Courts consider flight risk, offence gravity, and means. Keep the bail ruling, receipts, and review application copies.

title: Boda boda and motorbike theft
content: Report stolen motorbikes with registration, engine and chassis numbers, and tracker data where fitted. Alert stages and mechanics with photos. Keep logbook copies, sale agreements, and OB records.

title: Burglary and housebreaking
content: Breaking into homes or shops to steal attracts burglary charges. Preserve the scene where possible, photograph forced entry, and list stolen items with values and receipts. Report the same day for OB entry.

title: Cattle rustling and banditry
citation: Penal Code; National Police Service operations guidance
content: Rustling and bandit attacks should be reported immediately with locations, numbers, and movement direction for security response. Communities should use peace committees and early warning. Keep OB numbers and loss lists.

title: Child neglect and abandonment
content: Failing to provide for a child or abandoning one can attract criminal and care proceedings. Report to children officers and police with birth records and evidence of neglect. Keep school, medical, and support-payment records.

title: Child sexual exploitation material
citation: Sexual Offences Act; Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act
content: Creating or sharing sexual images of children is a grave offence. Do not forward such material; report to police and the DCI child-protection units with links and handles. Keep report references safely.

title: Demands for bribes by officials
citation: Anti-Corruption and Economic Crimes Act, 2003; Bribery Act, 2016
content: Demands for bribes for services, licences, or release can be reported to EACC with dates, amounts, and recordings where lawfully obtained. Do not pay to speed up a right. Keep receipts and reference numbers.

title: Fake currency encounters
citation: Penal Code; Central Bank of Kenya Act
content: Notes suspected to be counterfeit should not be re-spent. Report to police and the bank with details of who gave them. Keep the transaction records and suspect description.

title: Cyber harassment and non-consensual images
content: Sharing intimate images without consent, cyberbullying, and threats online are offences. Preserve links with timestamps, report to the platform and police, and seek support services. Do not delete evidence.

title: Defilement of children: urgent steps
content: Defilement cases need immediate medical care, preferably within 72 hours, and prompt police reporting. Do not wash away evidence before examination. The child needs counselling, a children officer referral, and legal aid. Keep medical and OB records.

title: Assault within the home: immediate steps
citation: Protection Against Domestic Violence Act, 2015; Penal Code
content: Seek safety and medical care first, then report to police for OB and P3 documentation. Protection orders can bar the abuser from the home. Keep medical records, photos, and witness details.

title: Drug possession and trafficking
citation: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1994
content: Possession and trafficking of narcotics attract severe penalties with limited bail options for trafficking. Anyone arrested should get counsel immediately and note the search and seizure details. Keep charge sheets and hearing dates.

title: Child marriage is prohibited
content: Marriage of a person under 18 is prohibited and voidable. Threatened marriages can be stopped through children officers, chiefs, and courts. Keep birth records, school records, and any ceremony plans as evidence.

title: Unlicensed guns and imitation firearms
content: Possession of firearms without a certificate, including imitation guns used in robberies, is a serious offence. Report armed sightings with descriptions and direction of movement without confronting. Keep report references.

title: Abuse and exploitation of older persons
content: Beating, neglecting, or grabbing property of older persons can be reported to chiefs, police, and social development officers. Arrange medical care and safe custody of documents. Keep medical and property records.

title: Obtaining by false pretences (wash-wash style fraud)
content: Con tricks promising jobs, tenders, or forex in exchange for fees are obtaining by false pretences. Stop further payments, preserve chats and receipts, and report to police and DCI. Keep adverts and suspect contacts.

title: FGM as a criminal offence
citation: Prohibition of Female Genital Mutilation Act, 2011
content: FGM, aiding it, or taking a girl across borders for it are offences. Suspected plans can be reported to police, chiefs, children officers, or helplines before the act. Keep any messages, plans, and witness details safely.

title: Forgery of documents
content: Making or using false title deeds, agreements, or certificates is forgery. Suspected forgeries should be reported with originals, the suspect documents, and transaction history. Keep registry search results and payment proof.

title: Protection orders for GBV survivors
content: Survivors can seek court protection orders barring contact, occupation, or tenancy interference. Applications are supported by affidavit evidence and police reports. Breach of an order is itself an offence. Keep the order and breach evidence.

title: Grievous harm and serious injury
content: Serious injuries such as fractures or deep wounds are prosecuted as grievous harm with heavy penalties. Hospital records and the P3 form are central evidence. Keep admission records, X-rays, and expense receipts.

title: Hate speech and incitement reports
content: Ethnic contempt, incitement, and hate leaflets can be reported to police or the NCIC with recordings and witness details. Keep originals of posts, broadcasts, and rally details for investigators.

title: Human trafficking indicators and reporting
content: False job offers, confiscated passports, and locked accommodation signal trafficking. Victims and witnesses can report to police, the counter-trafficking secretariat, or helplines. Keep messages, contracts, travel documents, and payment records.

title: Identity theft and fake IDs
citation: Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, 2018; Penal Code
content: Use of another person's ID for loans or SIM registration is identity theft. Victims should report to police and DCI, notify lenders and CRB, and dispute fraudulent accounts in writing. Keep affidavits and dispute letters.

title: Illicit brew and unlicensed alcohol
content: Manufacturing or selling chang'aa or unlicensed alcohol is an offence enforced with county officers and police. Report dens to chiefs and police rather than confronting sellers. Keep report references.

title: Kidnapping and abduction response
content: Report missing or abducted persons immediately with photos, clothing details, last location, and phone data. Police can seek call data through proper channels. Keep the OB number and investigating officer contacts.

title: Reporting lost documents and items
content: Lost IDs, certificates, and number plates should be reported promptly for an OB entry and police abstract needed for replacement. Keep the abstract copy for the registrar or NTSA.

title: Malicious damage to property
content: Damaging windows, fences, crops, or vehicles can be charged as malicious damage. Photograph the damage, get repair estimates, and report with ownership proof. Keep receipts for all repairs.

title: Mob justice is a crime: what to do
content: Beating or killing suspects is murder or assault regardless of the accusation. Witnesses should report to police and preserve photos safely. Communities should hand suspects to lawful custody.

title: M-Pesa reversal and fraud scams
content: Fake reversal calls and wrong-number refunds are common fraud. Never share PINs, verify balances independently, and report with transaction codes to the provider and police. Keep SMS records and call reference numbers.

title: Murder and manslaughter procedure
citation: Penal Code, Cap. 63; Criminal Procedure Code
content: Homicide cases begin with immediate police report, scene preservation, and post-mortem examination. Only the High Court tries murder. Families should get the OB number, post-mortem report access, and legal aid early.

title: Online shopping and social media fraud
content: Fake online sellers vanish after payment. Screenshot listings, seller profiles, till numbers, and chats before they disappear, then report to the platform, provider, and DCI. Keep payment confirmations.

title: Stolen phones: IMEI and tracking
content: Report phone theft with the IMEI, block the SIM with the provider, and give police the box and purchase receipt. Court orders may be needed for tracking data. Keep the OB number and provider references.

title: Plea bargaining in criminal cases
citation: Criminal Procedure Code; ODPP plea-bargain guidelines
content: Accused persons may negotiate pleas with the prosecution through counsel, subject to court approval. Agreements must be voluntary and informed. Never plead without understanding the sentence. Keep the agreement and court record.

title: Assault by police: where to complain
content: Excessive force, shootings, or deaths in custody can be reported to IPOA with station, date, OB details, and medical evidence. Parallel complaints may go to KNCHR. Keep medical reports, photos, and witness contacts.

title: Reporting rape and adult sexual assault
content: Survivors should reach safety, seek medical care, and report to police for P3 and statement recording. Counselling and PEP treatment have strict time windows. Keep clothes worn, messages, and witness details for investigators.

title: Police clearance certificate (good conduct)
content: Good-conduct applications run through eCitizen with fingerprints at designated centres. Delays are followed up with the application reference. Keep the payment receipt and fingerprint acknowledgement.

title: Robbery and violent theft
content: Robbery involving force or threats is a grave offence with severe penalties. Victims should seek safety and medical care first, then report with descriptions, plate numbers, and recovered items. Do not confront armed suspects.

title: Shoplifting and supermarket theft
content: Shop theft is prosecuted with CCTV, recovered goods, and staff testimony. Suspects should cooperate with police and seek counsel early. Keep the OB entry and charge sheet copies.

title: SIM-swap fraud response
citation: Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, 2018; KICA
content: Sudden loss of network followed by strange withdrawals signals SIM swap. Contact the telco to freeze the line, notify banks, and report to DCI with IDs and transaction records. Keep reference numbers from every office.

title: Stock theft and livestock movement
citation: Penal Code; livestock movement permit rules
content: Stolen cattle, goats, and sheep cases need ownership marks, photos, and movement records. Report the same day and alert neighbouring markets and slaughter points. Keep branding certificates and sale records.

title: Attempted suicide: help not punishment
content: Persons in crisis need urgent care, counselling, and helpline support rather than stigma. Contact emergency services, counsellors, or helplines such as 1199 or 0800 720 640 referrals. Keep referral records for follow-up care.

title: Theft: reporting and what police need
content: Theft of phones, livestock, or household goods should be reported promptly with serial numbers, purchase receipts, and witness names. Obtain the OB number and follow up with the investigating officer. Keep the OB slip and any recovery documents.

title: Threats to kill or harm
content: Written or uttered threats of death or injury are offences. Preserve messages with timestamps, report to police, and request advice on protection. Keep screenshots, call logs, and witness names.

title: Night trespass and prowling
content: Lurking around homes at night with intent can be charged as night trespass. Report with times, descriptions, and CCTV where available. Improve lighting and locks while police investigate.

title: Victim impact statements at sentencing
content: Victims may present impact statements on harm suffered before sentencing. Prepare the statement with medical, financial, and emotional effects. Keep expense receipts and reports to attach.

title: Wildlife and charcoal offences
citation: Wildlife Conservation and Management Act, 2013; Forest Conservation Act
content: Poaching, bushmeat trade, and illegal logging or charcoal burning attract heavy fines and jail terms enforced with KWS and KFS. Report quietly with locations and vehicle details. Keep report numbers.

title: Witness protection for serious crimes
content: Threatened witnesses in serious cases can seek protection through the Witness Protection Agency via police or ODPP. Report threats immediately with details. Keep threat evidence and agency references.

title: Wrongful arrest and malicious prosecution
content: Arrests without cause or fabricated charges can ground compensation claims after acquittal. Note every detail of the arrest, bond, and trial outcome. A lawyer assesses prospects once proceedings conclude.

title: Escalating cases through DCI and ODPP — general guidance
citation: National Police Service Act; Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions Act
content: Complex or stalled criminal complaints in Kenya can be escalated from the police station to DCI offices, with prosecution decisions made independently by the ODPP. Complainants can follow up in writing and request reasons for delays or decisions. Keep OB numbers, statements, and all follow-up letters.

title: Hate speech and NCIC complaints — general guidance
content: Hate speech and incitement along ethnic, racial, or religious lines are prohibited in Kenya and can be reported to police or the National Cohesion and Integration Commission. Online posts, broadcasts, and public rallies can all form the basis of complaints. Keep screenshots, recordings, and report reference numbers.

title: P3 forms and medical evidence after assault — general guidance
content: Victims of assault or sexual offences in Kenya should seek prompt medical care and have injuries documented through a police-issued P3 form completed by a medical officer. Early treatment and documentation help preserve evidence even where reporting is delayed. Keep hospital notes, P3 forms, and OB numbers.

title: Criminal procedure — general guidance
content: Criminal cases generally start with a report to police, investigation, arrest or summons, plea, hearing, and judgment. An accused person should be informed of the charge, may seek bail or bond, and should get legal representation early. Keep the charge sheet, bond documents, and hearing dates.

title: Wildlife offences and KWS enforcement — general guidance
content: Poaching, trafficking in trophies, and unauthorised entry into protected areas attract serious penalties enforced with Kenya Wildlife Service support. Community members can report suspicious activity to KWS or police without confronting suspects. Keep report numbers and any permits or receipts.

title: Fraud and obtaining by false pretences — general guidance
content: Fraud, obtaining money by false pretences, and forgery are criminal offences. Preserve M-Pesa messages, bank statements, contracts, IDs used, and call records, and report promptly to police and, for online cases, the DCI. Do not send more money to recover the loss without advice.

title: Gender-based violence reporting — general guidance
content: Survivors of gender-based violence should prioritise safety and medical care, then report to police and request a P3 form and referral to legal aid and psychosocial support. Keep medical records, torn clothing as evidence where advised, messages, and witness details. The National Legal Aid Service line is 0800 720 640.

title: Criminal mention and plea in Magistrates Courts — general guidance
content: Criminal cases are first mentioned for plea-taking, bail consideration and directions on disclosure and witnesses. Adjourned mentions track investigations and readiness for hearing. Keep the bail order, bond receipts and mention dates recorded.

title: P3 medical examination form — general guidance
citation: National Police Service and health guidance
content: In assault or injury cases, police issue a P3 form for examination and documentation by a medical officer. The completed form supports investigation and prosecution. Keep a copy of the issued and returned P3 records.

title: Penal Code (Cap. 63)
content: The Penal Code defines criminal offences in Kenya and their penalties, including assault, theft, fraud, and property offences, and sets out general principles of criminal liability. Criminal cases are prosecuted by the State through the Director of Public Prosecutions; victims report to police and keep OB numbers, medical reports, and receipts.

title: Police OB entry and police abstract — general guidance
content: Incidents such as accidents, loss or assault should be reported promptly at a police station for entry in the Occurrence Book. A police abstract summarises the report for insurance or court use. Keep the OB number and abstract copy safely.

title: Sentencing, probation and community service — general guidance
citation: Probation of Offenders Act; Community Service Orders Act
content: Courts may impose fines, imprisonment, probation, or community service depending on the offence. First-time and minor offenders may be considered for non-custodial sentences. Verify the sentence, payment deadlines, and reporting conditions on the court order.

title: Reporting crime: OB, DCI and ODPP — general guidance
content: Report crime at the nearest police station and obtain the OB number. Serious or cyber-enabled cases may be escalated to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations. Prosecution decisions rest with the Director of Public Prosecutions. Keep OB numbers, statements, and exhibit receipts.

title: Sexual Offences Act, 2006
content: The Sexual Offences Act defines sexual offences, penalties, victim support, and reporting procedures. Survivors should seek safety and medical care promptly, report to police, and preserve evidence. Support includes psychosocial care, P3 medical forms, and legal aid referral.
